subject: ctmm.boot error and increasing computational efficiency

messages.author: 78a562fca03c4fee
messages.subject: ctmm.boot error and increasing computational efficiency
parts:
Hello,

Big thanks to this group for all of the great questions and information, particularly Chris for your endless help and responsiveness.

I am attempting to calculate AKDEs for several individuals within a population, and hoping to calculate a PKDE as well. Similar to the gazelles in the Fleming et al 2019 supplement, the species I’m working with has very few range crossings (N << n), some with DOFs of 5-8, while others have DOFs of 2-4. Total observations (GPS fixes) range from ~600-4,000. For those individuals with DOFs <5 I am attempting to use ctmm.boot to run the parametric bootstrap; however, I have a few questions:

Firstly, I installed the latest development version of ctmm from the Git repository, and when I run ctmm.boot(telemetry, fit[[1]], iterate = TRUE, trace = TRUE) I receive the following error: 

Error in !POS : invalid argument type. 

I uninstalled this version and reinstalled the package from CRAN, and ran the same code without error. I repeated this process on two computers with the same results, so it seems there may be an issue with ctmm.boot in the most recent version (?) Has anyone else encountered this?

Secondly, I understand the function is computationally expensive. It has been running for about 6 days for one individual with ~2500 observations. It’s still only at 83% percent and likely needs to go through additional iterations. In Fleming et al 2019, they state 'relative error <<5% will become computationally wasteful', whereas I believe the default is 1%. Should I change this to 5%? Alternatively, given the computational cost, would it be advisable to switch iterate = FALSE and/or thin my data? Not sure if that would reduce computation time, but, again, the animals cross their range on a seasonal basis, and I have 4hr fix rates, which seems like overkill given the range crossing frequency.

Any insights would be greatly appreciated.

Thank you,

Tyler

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: ctmm.boot error and increasing computational efficiency
parts:
Hi Tyler,

If you can please send me a minimal working example that can replicate that error, then I can take a look at it. I just added a feature to ctmm.boot so that you can safely increase the error argument without the variance estimates becoming noisy. That probably introduced a bug.

That statement from Fleming et al. (2019) is explaining that its wasteful to set the numerical error target (the error argument) to be much lower than the relative bias of O(1/DOF^3) that the bootstrapped pHREML estimate can obtain.

error=0.05 will be 25 times faster than the default of error=0.01. iterate=FALSE will also be a couple of times faster. Sampling intervals much smaller than the range crossing timescale are going to give you diminishing returns in the home-range estimation. Finally, I will add that ctmm.boot is one of the functions in ctmm that is parallelized with the cores argument. If you have 8 cores, then you can turn that up to run 8 times faster, as bootstrapping is embarrassingly parallelizable.

Best,
Chris

This issue should be fixed on Github now.

Thinning will speed things up linearly, but I would try using multiple cores and turning iterate off before resorting to that.

Best,
Chris
